video_goal: Demonstrate how to visually authenticate a Series 2013 $100 bill by inspecting the 3D Security Ribbon and color-shifting ink features.
required_subjects_and_props: Series 2013 $100 bill, dark table surface, bright directional light source

outline_steps.visual_action: Place the Series 2013 $100 bill flat on a dark, well-lit table, ensuring the front side with Benjamin Franklin is facing up.
Hands pick up the bill by the left and right edges, lifting it toward the camera lens into the light.
The right index finger traces the vertical blue 3D Security Ribbon running down the center-right of the bill to highlight its position.
Fingers pinch and slightly bend the paper around the blue 3D Security Ribbon to visually demonstrate that the ribbon is woven into the paper, not printed on top.
Tilt the top edge of the bill back and forth. The tiny bells inside the blue 3D Security Ribbon visually change into '100's as the angle changes.
Tilt the bill side to side from left to right. The '100' icons inside the blue 3D Security Ribbon move up and down in response to the side-to-side motion.
The index finger moves to the right of the ribbon and points directly at the copper-colored inkwell containing a bell icon.
Tilt the bill back and forth. The bell inside the inkwell shifts color from copper to green, making it appear to vanish into the background of the inkwell.
The index finger slides down to point at the large '100' numeral located in the bottom right corner of the bill.
Tilt the bill up and down again. The color-shifting ink on the large '100' numeral transitions smoothly from copper to green.
Hold the bill up directly against the bright directional light source to reveal the hidden faint watermark of Benjamin Franklin's face on the far right side.
Place the verified Series 2013 $100 bill back onto the dark table and smooth it flat with both hands.
